newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA MOSER APPROVES IFC INVESTMENT.
newsitem.headline: INDIA MOSER APPROVES IFC INVESTMENT.

text.p: India's Moser Baer Ltd on Monday approved a plan to issue preferential shares worth 20.2 million rupees ($566,620) to the World Bank's private sector financing arm International Finance Corporation (IFC).
"The board of the company has approved the IFC investment. We will now seek shareholders' approval on September 20," Ratul Puri, manager, business development, told Reuters.
He said the price per share would be fixed according to the guidelines laid down by the Securities and Exchange Board of India. "We expect each share to sell for between 15 and 20 rupees."
Moser Baer makes computer discs in technical collaboration with Germany's BASF AG on the outskirts of the Indian capital. The company has a capital base of 143.9 million rupees.
Promoters hold 45 percent equity, financial institutions hold 15 percent and the rest is held by the public.
The investment was part of an expansion plan, Puri said.
"We are increasing our disc manufacturing capacity from 12 million a year to 84 million," he said.

Puri said Moser Baer is in the process of establishing a technical collaboration with Korea's Samsung Electronics for making optical storage devices like recordable digital video discs and compact discs.
"We will be investing 1.5 billion rupees in the optical storage device plant."
